differentiator_evidence.evidence: Multiple mobile apps focus on academic questions; at least one explicitly says practical training is not covered.
Public reviews of an existing paid app complain that questions are too easy or unlike the real exam wording.
Paid courses and practical DVDs show spending on practical preparation, but not on this exact workflow.

acquisition_evidence.evidence: Several exam-prep apps and reviews exist, but practical/oral query volume and attainable ranking are not measured.

unknowns: legal right to use current practical rubrics

kill_criteria: No legally usable and current practical/oral rubric
Fewer than 10 repeated public complaints about solo practical/oral practice
No measurable acquisition demand beyond academic quiz searches
Annual reachable market cannot support at least 816 one-time sales at JPY 2980
Qualified content review would create ongoing per-customer or high fixed labor
An exact speech-scored competitor is found with 70 percent or greater workflow overlap
reason: Paid exam-prep behavior and an apparent practical-training gap exist, but exact demand, content rights, accuracy, distribution and economics are not yet proven. Implementation remains prohibited.
